source.ctx_pruned_to_read_nodes: ctx holds only the nodes compile-current-state actually reads via $('...'); the other 34-51 nodes that ran in this execution were dropped so the fixture fits the 400 KB budget. `ran` still lists every node, in real execution order. No node the body reads was removed - dym-annotate / dym-annotate-partial / patch-transcript / cs-roster-plan did not run in any of these three executions.
source.rationale: THE DEFECT, CAPTURED. Clone execution 13498401 (2026-08-22T13:22Z, txiPzSxy3Pclsz6v), the turn "check stock for SRTWC286-SH and RMA-SRT2608-011", run AFTER resolve-entity began stripping [-\s]+ from product tokens. `expected` is deliberately NOT the recorded output: the recorded reply reported only "Sorrento kitchen sink" and dropped the RMA-SRT2608-011 miss entirely, under a 48-row stock answer. resolve-entity was sent RMASRT2608011; the old suppression rule asked whether that exact string appeared in qf.entities[].raw (where it reads RMA-SRT2608-011), concluded the CRM had invented the token, and silenced a genuine miss - the failure UAC SR-U5 forbids. The rule is now POSITIVE: a resolution is only treated as the CRM's own appended query-sentence when it HAS matches and every one of them carries match_tier "spec_search". Neither miss qualifies, so both are reported. Everything above "Couldn't find these:" is byte-identical to the recorded reply, and the separator is live's ": not found.". KNOWN RESIDUAL, pinned as-is on purpose: the miss line quotes RMASRT2608011, the resolver's stripped echo, not the customer's RMA-SRT2608-011. That is the same class of defect the search-scope header's casing fix and not-found-error-message's _rawOfTok address, on a third renderer neither covers. It is a separate copy decision and is NOT fixed here - this fixture records it rather than hiding it.
